content.title: THE HEALTHY COOKING {{MISTAKES}} YOU DON'T NOTICE
facts: Broccoli – **boiling** it for several minutes leaches water-soluble nutrients into the pot; a quick **steam** keeps far more intact.
Onions – chopping and cooking them **immediately** cuts off time for beneficial sulfur compounds to form; let cut onion **rest** for a few minutes first.
Sweet Potatoes – peeling before cooking tosses out much of the **fiber** concentrated right under the skin; cook them **unpeeled** when you can.
Blueberries – washing them right after buying speeds up mold growth and nutrient loss; rinse **just before eating**, not before **storing**.
Olive Oil – heating it to a high smoke point breaks down its **polyphenols**; save good extra virgin oil for finishing dishes or **low-heat** cooking.
Asparagus – snapping off and discarding the thick ends removes a good chunk of the stalk's **fiber**; trim less and cook the tougher parts a bit longer instead.
